ManifestoOne run, twenty metres
We don't build model cars. We build a twenty-metre argument.

Twenty metres, one cartridge, no corners. There is nowhere for a bad decision to hide, so every surface has to be justified with data before it is cut.

Race time and championship position stay empty until the season writes them — we are not filling this page with figures we have not earned.

Aerodynamics

Wing profiles developed against flow-trajectory studies. Target: attached flow off the trailing edge, vortices passing outboard of the rear wheels.

Chassis

A single machined model-board body carrying the cartridge chamber, tether line and axle mounts, checked against the regulations in CAD before any toolpath.

Propulsion

One 8 g CO₂ cartridge, pierced at the start gate. Everything after that is mass, alignment and rolling resistance — where most of the run is actually won.

Manufacturing

CNC body, printed aero surfaces, bearing-mounted wheels, hand-filled and sprayed. Tolerance and surface quality are performance items, not cosmetics.

Engineeringp. 12

Five disciplines. One machine.

Regulation study, three competing body concepts, then one parametric solid model. Packaging the cartridge chamber and tether line shapes the car long before aerodynamics gets a say.

Aerodynamics

Flow studies run in SolidWorks Flow Simulation over eighty solver iterations, plotted as velocity in Z. The side view shows separation; the head-on view shows the vortex structures.

Toolpaths from the frozen model, blank cut on the CNC, wings printed and cleaned up, then filled, sanded and sprayed by hand. The finish is measured, not judged by eye.

Manufacturing
Precision
Material

Rolling resistance, launch repeatability and wheel alignment measured against the simulation's predictions. Where they disagree, the simulation gets rebuilt — not the logbook.

Data

Refinement

Twenty metres, judged alongside the portfolio, the pit display and the verbal presentation. A season of analysis resolves into roughly one second of running.

    Partners and contactp. 30

    Build with us.

    Materials, machining and printing are the constraint on how many revisions we get to run. Partners lift that ceiling directly.

    Who we are

    A student-led STEM Racing team from Kingswood School, Bath — designing, simulating, machining and racing our own CO₂-powered car.

    Why partners matter

    Every design revision costs model board, machine time and print material. The budget decides how many ideas reach the track.

    What support enables

    More iterations cut, tested and validated against simulation before race day — and competition costs covered.

    What partners receive

    Credit on the car, the pit display, team kit, the portfolio and this site, scaled to the level of partnership.

    Partnership levelsAvailability

    Title

    Naming position on the car and in the team name. Primary placement across livery, pit display, kit and portfolio.

    One

    Technical

    Materials, machining, printing, software or engineering mentorship — credited on the car and in the portfolio.

    Two

    Supporting

    Contribution towards competition costs, credited on the car, the pit display and this site.
